title: Radiography - Joan Patterson
writingTask:
Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter to Dr Richard Lyle, Consultant Breast Surgeon, Westend Breast Assessment Clinic, 2 Hospital Avenue, Westend, reporting the mammographic findings and requesting urgent assessment of the patient.

In your answer:
- Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
- Do not use note form
- Use letter format

The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
caseNotes: Mrs Joan Patterson attended the Westend Breast Screening Unit for a routine screening mammogram
The images show an abnormality requiring urgent assessment
Patient DOB: 30 May 1957
Social background: retired teacher, married
Social background: non-smoker, minimal alcohol
Social background: active, regular walking

Medical history: osteoarthritis of the hands and knees
Medical history: no previous breast surgery or biopsy
Medical history: never used HRT
Reason for attendance: routine breast screening via national programme invitation
Reason for attendance: asymptomatic, no palpable lump reported
Reason for attendance: no nipple discharge or skin changes
Reason for attendance: no breast pain
Current background: previous screening in 2016 reported normal
Current background: attends regularly for screening
Current background: aware of family history, understandably anxious
Screening: no breast implants
Screening: pregnancy not applicable, post-menopausal
Screening: no recent breast trauma
Imaging performed: bilateral digital mammography, CC and MLO views
Imaging performed: adequate compression, good image quality
Imaging findings: 1.5cm spiculated mass in the left breast, upper outer quadrant
Imaging findings: associated clustered microcalcifications
Imaging findings: right breast normal, no abnormal density
Imaging findings: graded suspicious of malignancy (M4/M5)
Impression/diagnosis: mammographic appearances suspicious of malignancy, requiring triple assessment

candidateLetter:
Dr Richard Lyle
Westend Breast Assessment Clinic
Westend

14 March 2019

Dear Dr Richard,

Re: Mrs Joan Patterson

I am writing to you about Mrs Joan Patterson. She is a retired teacher and she is married. She has osteoarthritis in her hands and knees. She come to the Westend Breast Screening Unit for her routine screening mammogram after an invitation from the national programme. Her previous screening in 2016 was normal.

Digital mammogram done both breasts, CC and MLO views. The compression was adequate and the image quality was good. We found a 2.5cm spiculated mass in the left breast, upper outer quadrant, it is suspicious. Unfortunatly, the mammogram shows that she has breast cancer. She said she found a small lump herself last month but did'nt tell anyone. She has no nipple discharge, skin changes or pain.

Patient recalled. We told her that recall does not always mean cancer, but she is really really worried. I think she needs to be seen by you. Please do the needful. Also, her sister had breast cancer at age 58.

Thanks a lot for your help!!

Yours faithfully,

Radiographer
Westend Breast Screening Unit
